annotation.authors_or_issuer: China University of Political Science and Law author(s)
annotation.summary_en: Article arguing Chinese accident law cannot accommodate humanoid robot accidents given hybrid human-algorithm control, adaptive learning and human-like embodiment. It proposes a reconstructed liability system: evidentiary processes with event data recorders and audits, a "reasonable person" technical standard, manufacturers as least cost avoiders, and behavioral correction or retribution for robots.
annotation.title_clean: Reconstructing Liability Mechanism for Humanoid Robot Accidents
annotation.title_en: Reconstructing Liability Mechanism for Humanoid Robot Accidents
key_provisions_or_claims: Existing Chinese accident law inadequately handles fault, causation, proof and remedy for humanoid robot accidents.
Require event data recorders (black boxes) and ex post third-party algorithmic testing and auditing.
Adopt a 'reasonable person' technical standard for humanoid robot behavior.
Designate manufacturers as least cost avoiders bearing primary liability.
Consider behavioral correction and retribution for robots to meet victims' psychological needs.
